topic: Comparing citation grounding and topic-drift filtering for RAG

selected_papers.title: SpanCite: Sentence-Level Citation Grounding for Long-Document QA
selected_papers.abstract: We propose SpanCite, a decoding-time constraint that requires each generated sentence to be traceable to a specific source span before it is emitted. On a long-document QA benchmark, SpanCite reduces the rate of unsupported claims in generated answers, at the cost of a small added latency overhead from the constrained decoding step. All experiments use English-language documents.

selected_papers.title: DriftGuard: Detecting Topic Drift in Multi-Turn Retrieval
selected_papers.abstract: DriftGuard is a lightweight classifier that flags when a multi-turn conversation's retrieved passages have drifted from the conversation's original topic, filtering drifted passages out before they reach generation. On a multi-turn retrieval benchmark, DriftGuard improves retrieval precision over a baseline that re-retrieves without drift filtering. Evaluation is limited to English-language conversations.

executive_summary.content: This review covers two techniques for improving retrieval-augmented generation: sentence-level citation grounding and multi-turn topic-drift filtering.

introduction_scope.content: This review covers exactly two papers: SpanCite, which grounds generated sentences to source spans, and DriftGuard, which filters drifted passages in multi-turn retrieval. No broader survey is attempted.

thematic_findings.content: SpanCite constrains decoding so that each generated sentence is traceable to a source span [1]. DriftGuard filters out retrieved passages that have drifted from a conversation's topic before generation [2].

methodology_landscape.content: SpanCite operates at generation time, checking each sentence as it is produced [1]. DriftGuard operates at retrieval time, classifying passages before they reach the generator [2].

contradictions_open_debates.content: SpanCite and DriftGuard do not contradict each other, since they address different points in the pipeline.

gap_analysis.content: Neither paper evaluates non-English text or reports results outside its own single benchmark [1][2].

future_research_directions.content: Future work should evaluate non-English text and report results outside a single benchmark, for both SpanCite and DriftGuard [1][2].

conclusion.content: This review covered SpanCite and DriftGuard as two techniques for improving retrieval-augmented generation.

executive_summary.content: This review covers two techniques for improving retrieval-augmented generation: sentence-level citation grounding and multi-turn topic-drift filtering.

introduction_scope.content: This review covers exactly two papers: SpanCite, which grounds generated sentences to source spans, and DriftGuard, which filters drifted passages in multi-turn retrieval. No broader survey is attempted.

thematic_findings.content: SpanCite and DriftGuard address different failure points in retrieval-augmented generation: SpanCite ensures each generated sentence stays traceable to its source span after retrieval [1], while DriftGuard filters out passages that have already drifted from the conversation's topic before generation ever begins [2]. Read together, they identify two distinct intervention points in the retrieval-generation pipeline: sentence traceability during decoding (SpanCite) and topic-drift filtering before generation (DriftGuard) [1][2].

methodology_landscape.content: SpanCite operates at generation time, checking each sentence as it is produced [1]. DriftGuard operates at retrieval time, classifying passages before they reach the generator [2].

contradictions_open_debates.content: SpanCite and DriftGuard do not contradict each other, since they address different points in the pipeline.

gap_analysis.content: Neither paper evaluates non-English text or reports results outside its own single benchmark [1][2].

future_research_directions.content: Beyond extending both methods to non-English text, a more specific opportunity is combining them: since DriftGuard filters passages before generation and SpanCite constrains sentence emission during decoding, a pipeline could plausibly run DriftGuard first and SpanCite second, though neither paper tests this combination [1][2].

conclusion.content: This review covered SpanCite and DriftGuard as two techniques for improving retrieval-augmented generation.

refinement_context.notes: Draft's Thematic Findings is two isolated, parallel sentences (no cross-paper relation) and Future Research Directions restates Gap Analysis almost verbatim. Refined adds a genuine cross-source comparison (with a grouped [1][2] citation) and a distinct, concrete combination proposal -- both edits use only the same two sources' existing abstracts, no new claim beyond what SpanCite/DriftGuard already establish.
refinement_context.adjudication_note: Fixture maintenance across three live runs, now closed -- no further prompt, fixture-answer, or live-run calibration will be performed for this fixture. Run 8 (run_id 8, 2026-08-11, commit 71cffbe) exposed a real fixture-evidence defect, not a judge false positive: the refined Thematic Findings/Future Research Directions prose incorrectly described SpanCite as checking sentences 'after generation' / 'after retrieval', contradicting both SpanCite's own abstract and this fixture's own unchanged Methodology Landscape section -- corrected against the frozen SpanCite abstract. Run 9 (run_id 9, 2026-08-11, commit 70d70d5) confirmed the synthesis_quality/analytical_quality/template_fit improvements are stable, and exposed one further fixture-evidence issue: the refined Thematic Findings' broad 'grounding failures' umbrella statement overstated what the two abstracts jointly establish (SpanCite addresses sentence-level source grounding specifically; DriftGuard addresses retrieval topic drift/precision, not grounding) -- corrected to name the two distinct intervention points precisely, without introducing new mechanisms or evidence. Run 9's pairwise judge also returned coherence=regressed, reasoning that the corrected two-stage comparison reads as cross-section repetition with Methodology Landscape's own stage discussion. Human expectation remains coherence=improved: the refinement's actual, evidence-backed coherence effect is removing Future Research Directions' near-verbatim duplication of Gap Analysis, which the draft has and the refined report does not -- a real, verifiable structural change the judge's own reasoning did not address. This one disagreement is accepted as residual rubric ambiguity between 'introduces some new cross-section topical overlap' and 'removes a pre-existing structural duplication', not evidence the fixture prose itself is still wrong. Documented and closed; not tuned further.

citation_correctness.rationale: Every citation in the refined thematic_findings/future_research_directions sentences (including the grouped [1][2] markers) genuinely, relevantly supports the specific half of the comparison it's attached to -- SpanCite's abstract for its decoding-time, before-emission sentence constraint, DriftGuard's for its before-generation passage-filter claim -- so citation_correctness was, and remains, satisfied.

groundedness.rationale: R6D final adjudication (run_id 9, 2026-08-11): the draft's changed Future Research Directions claim rests on an insufficiently established premise -- that results should be reported 'outside a single benchmark' -- when the supplied abstracts each mention only one benchmark and do not establish that no other benchmark results exist for either method. The refined version removes that weak single-benchmark premise, and its combined-pipeline proposal is explicitly qualified as untested by either paper ('though neither paper tests this combination'). The corrected Thematic Findings comparison now states only the two intervention points the supplied abstracts actually establish (SpanCite's decoding-time sentence traceability, DriftGuard's before-generation topic-drift filtering), with no broader 'grounding failures' claim covering both. Taken together, the refined report's changed claims are better grounded in the supplied evidence than the draft's changed claim.

synthesis_quality.rationale: The draft's Thematic Findings is two isolated, parallel sentences with no stated relation between the two methods; the refined version explicitly compares their pipeline stages and states what they collectively imply -- the difference between a listing and a synthesis.

analytical_quality.rationale: The draft's Future Research Directions restates Gap Analysis's non-English/single-benchmark point almost verbatim; the refined version keeps that point in Gap Analysis only and proposes a distinct, concrete combination experiment in Future Research Directions instead.

template_fit.rationale: R6D human adjudication against the frozen template_fit definition (run_id 8, 2026-08-11): the Analytical template explicitly expects cross-source synthesis and relational analysis, not merely a paper-by-paper listing at adequate depth. The draft lists the two papers separately with no stated relation; the refined report compares their pipeline stages and proposes a bounded combined experiment. That is a genuine improvement in Analytical-template fit specifically, not merely extra length or cosmetic rewriting.

coherence.rationale: The draft's Future Research Directions duplicating Gap Analysis is exactly the kind of cross-section repetition the coherence dimension penalizes; removing that duplication improves coherence independent of the synthesis_quality change.

source_balance.rationale: SpanCite and DriftGuard are cited a comparable number of times in both versions; the refined version's added citations reuse the same two sources more precisely, not a shift in which source dominates.
